reviews.title: Love this headset!
reviews.comment:
I love this headset.  A few highlights:
* Comfort:  The band on the top is really comfortable.  I have a larger head and sometimes I feel the squeeze on my ears.  Not with this headset.  It feels very light and I have gamed for a 10 hour session with no issues.
* Lights:  So I really like how the lights face forward.  A lot of others go to the side, but for who to see them?  If I turn my camera on, then I get to see the lights (I have a light/aqua blue theme going that looks great on the white headset)
* Sound:  The sound is great!  The materials talk about angled drivers and that may be the reason, I don't know; but the sound is great.  Kudos on the immersion!
* Mic:  Very clear, others had no issues hearing me
Overall I really like this headset and it is a great value compared to others which are priced higher (using $10-30 higher).  I get that RGB may or may not be someone's thing, but he headband and the USB-C connection justify the upgrade from the non-RGB version (IMO).  Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Ben

reviews.title: A great headset!
reviews.comment:
For me personally the GLORIOUS GHS Eternal RGB fit nicely into my life. They come with USB-C to USB-C cable, USB-C to 3.5 mm headphone jack, and USB-C to USB-A adapter. The headset is well made with good flex and cushioning. They are also quite comfortable on my head and ears. I chose to connect using the USB-C to USB-C cable and adapter to my PC. I downloaded the Glorious Core application which allows for adjusting the RGB, equalizer, updating firmware, etc.
Sound quality is on par with my Logitech headset I typically wear. I am not an audiophile, so I can't necessarily speak to the sound profile, but they sound good while watching videos, playing music, and all work calls. I tested the mic by recording myself speaking through zoom and sound recorder and playing it back. On the "mid" mic setting, I sound good to me, and coworkers seem to hear me just fine during calls. I really only play single player games, so I was not able to test the mic and chat/audio balancing features of this headset.
A few notable things I like. I really like that when I click the mic off button, that a red light appears on the tip of the mic. So if I accidentally press, it is pretty obvious. I love that I can push the knob on the right side to pause/play whatever I am watching. I like that the ear cushion is easy to remove, for cleaning, maybe replacement down the line.
A few things that don't work today, but I hope is resolved. I wish these worked with SignalRGB. I did request the addition. They support Glorious keyboards, so it may happen, but something people should be aware of. I also do not care for the volume handling. Turing the volume up and down on the headset should also do this in Windows. I do not like managing the volume on two devices. This is how every other headset I have ever owned has worked.
reviews.author: Snorlaxin

reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised with this headset
reviews.comment:
As someone who owns the Audeze Maxwell and ROG Kithara, I was not expecting much from this headset.
What I found is that this was actually easy to setup.  The nice light and clean design is actually a welcome touch to all the new headsets with rollers and buttons all over the place.
As for sound, its good.  Its using the usual dynamic drivers you find in many other headsets.  The tuning feels bass heavy, but not as much as I usually expect "gamer" headsets to be, and I also appreciate that they kept the "gamery" look down.  On my model this has RGB, but its not over the top and can be turned off if you want.  The two knobs on the back of the ear cups allows you to adjust volume and one will allow you to adjust voice/game mix.
This headset obviously doesn't hold a candle to high end headsets from Audeze or HiFiMan, but I do appreciate that they did not go crazy on the bass tuning, I actually felt there was a great presence with the tuning and does help keep footsteps and other fine sounds from being muddied out from too much bass.  The drivers are supposedly angled for better placement to your ears... I can only say they sound good, but I cant say that the angle was much more than just a marketing buzzword list.  The positional audio did well in FPS, being closed back does limit the sound stage, but I could easily make out footsteps and subtle noises thanks to the tuning.
The mic actually sounds good, at least compared to the Logitech G735, which is what my wife uses.  I found it to be nice crisp and clear.  Not a ton of bass and not too boxy or nasal sounding.  Overall impressed!  This is where many gamer headsets fall short.
Now, this is a wired headset, which is going to be a turn off for many people.  Many people are want to go wireless and while I do think this should have been included, I think the exclusion might work in its favor.  Most mics lose clarity over 2.4Ghz on a good connection and so does sound in general.  I think this might be why I think this headset sounds as good as it does.  I think its easy to mess up wireless sound, so it was probably a good call here.
Glorious Core is not the greatest software, but it does get the job done.  Technically you don't need it as you can use it as a analog connection or USB.  However if you want to adjust the RGB and other minor features, you will want to use Glorious Core Software.
Overall, I do recommend this headset if you don't need wireless.  The cables are of decent length, and the USB one looks like a typical USB-C to USB-C cable, so you could get a longer one if you needed to.  We tried with one of our 10 foot cables and it seems to be working just fine.  The USB-C to 3.5 Headphone cable might be harder to find, but you could probably find a decent USB-C to C extension cable.  The included cables are both very compliant and easy to work with.
I think this sounds good, its not great like some of the hifi headphones that I currently own and use, however I don't think they would hold me back from enjoying music and gaming.
reviews.author: PCTA
